questions.question: When turning, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off your signal just before you turn.
Signal only if other vehicles are ahead of you.

questions.explanation: Turn on your signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep the signal on during the entire turn. Turn it off after you finish turning if your car does not have self-canceling signals.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a construction worker near the road?

options.text: Do not drive in any lane.
Wait until construction is finished before driving.

questions.explanation: When driving through work zones, always reduce your speed when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, what can you do?

options.text: You might be able to drive onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You might be able to drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In some emergencies, driving onto the shoulder can help you avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support heavy vehicles.

questions.question: A distracted driver usually:

options.text: Follows the rules of the road.

questions.explanation: Distracted drivers notice hazards on the road more slowly than alert drivers, or they do not notice hazards at all.

questions.question: If your engine catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Turn off the engine right away.
Do not use a fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine right away.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as possible to stop the fire from spreading. Do not open the hood unless you need to.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Do not try to reach your destination while tired—it is dangerous. Coffee will not keep you safe.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, what is the safest speed to drive?

options.text: Slower than the traffic around you.
The same speed as the traffic around you.
Faster than the traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as the traffic around you.
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, drive at the same speed as other vehicles. When two vehicles drive in the same direction at the same speed, they cannot hit each other.

questions.question: The heavier a vehicle is:

options.text: The less important the brakes are.
The harder the brakes need to work.
The quieter the brakes will sound.

questions.correctAnswerText: The harder the brakes need to work.
questions.explanation: Heavy vehicles need stronger brakes to stop completely.

questions.question: Which one is NOT an example of a dangerous driver?

options.text: A driver who has not scraped ice off the windshield
The driver of a rental truck
The driver of a station wagon with items blocking the back windows
A person driving a pickup truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person driving a pickup truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards on the road. Examples include drivers with ice on their windshields, drivers with large items blocking windows, and drivers of rental trucks who are not used to limited rear visibility.

questions.question: What is black ice?

options.text: A thick layer of ice on the road
A thin layer of ice on the road
Ice that is black from dirt on the road
Ice that is easy to see

questions.correctAnswerText: A thin layer of ice on the road
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it may look like a wet road instead of ice.

questions.question: Are wheels with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Yes, if a professional did the repairs.
Yes, if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are not safe. They must be replaced before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand to keep the other hand free.
With one hand at a time, switching hands as needed.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: When checking the exhaust system, which of these is NOT a problem?

options.text: Exhaust system parts not rubbing against fuel system parts

questions.correctAnswerText: Exhaust system parts not rubbing against fuel system parts
questions.explanation: Watch for these exhaust system problems: loose, broken, or missing pipes, mufflers, or tailpipes; loose, broken, or missing brackets and bolts; exhaust parts rubbing against fuel system parts, tires, or other moving parts; and leaking exhaust parts.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of when to shift gears?

options.text: The speed of vehicles next to you

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of vehicles next to you
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift gears. First is engine speed (rpm)—read your manual to learn when to shift. Second is road speed (mph)—learn which speeds work with each gear and watch the speedometer.

questions.question: If oil and water build up in the air tanks, the brakes:
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks daily to remove water and oil. Too much oil and water can damage brake function.

questions.question: A driver who stops at a green light could be:
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of impaired driving, such as stopping in wrong places like at green lights. Impaired drivers may have used alcohol, drugs, or be sleepy or ill.

questions.question: When starting the engine for a pre-trip inspection, what should the driver do?

options.text: Put the engine in first gear.

questions.explanation: During the pre-trip inspection, start the engine and listen for unusual noises.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when used:
questions.explanation: Brakes that pull to one side show a brake problem and need to be checked.

questions.question: Front tire treads must be at least ____ deep in every major groove.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles need a tread depth of 4/32 of an inch in every major groove on front tires and 2/32 of an inch on other tires.

questions.question: Where should hazmat placards be placed on a truck?

options.text: On the left and right sides

questions.explanation: Hazmat placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.
